purpose: Visual design references inspected for report revision; not a literature review and not copied result curves
copyright_use: Downloaded originals retained for private visual inspection only. Recreate layout logic with our own geometry/data; do not paste other papers curves as project results.

references.authors: Jean-Jacques Greffet, Rémi Carminati, Karl Joulain, Jean-Philippe Mulet, Stéphane Mainguy, Yong Chen
references.title: Coherent emission of light by thermal sources
observations: Fig1 is a grayscale 3D AFM morphology with lateral micrometre and depth nanometre scales, so geometry and scale appear before optical performance.
Fig2 is an upper-half polar angular emission plot: 0 degrees at top normal, plus/minus90 at horizontal endpoints; radial axis is absolute emissivity.
Fig3 uses hollow markers for measured angular points over thin continuous calculation curves; fixed colors differentiate wavelengths.
Fig4 uses color to encode incidence angle and solid/dashed line type to distinguish experiment and theory; minimal grid, units on axes.
application: Place surface normal vertically upward in the angle schematic and in any polar coordinates.
Keep dimensions and materials visible next to every geometric comparison.
Use consistent colors for H or direction and marker/line type for s/p or simulation/prediction.
do_not_transfer: Do not copy SiC grating geometry or spectral curves to optical-Ti cavity results.
Only two solved directions exist in this batch; do not draw a continuous emission lobe, infer a FWHM, mirror negative angles, or make an angle-wavelength heatmap from them.

references.authors: Aaswath P. Raman, Marc Abou Anoma, Linxiao Zhu, Eden Rephaeli, Shanhui Fan
references.title: Passive radiative cooling below ambient air temperature under direct sunlight
observations: Fig1 places photograph, 3D operation schematic with arrows, cut-out cross section, and layer-resolved SEM/zoom in one a–d figure. Layer thicknesses are directly labeled.

Fig2 separates solar and mid-IR response into vertically aligned panels; the measured response is a thin dark blue line while reference spectra are low-contrast filled backgrounds with direct text labels.
Fig3 uses consistent blue for cooler and black for ambient, with direct curve labels; green irradiation is labeled with its own axis.
application: For this report assemble plan view, proportionate 3D geometry, and floorfill cross section into a coherent a–c group; show enlarged t inset explicitly if needed.
Use a consistent thin-line/marker style with labeled axes rather than large bars; use low-contrast backgrounds only for a valid known reference.
do_not_transfer: Our current result is at10.5um; an illustrative8–13um shaded window must not imply a computed continuous spectrum.
Do not insert AM1.5 or atmospheric-transmittance curves without source/condition information and a purpose relevant to the calculation.

references.title: Nanophotonic particle simulation and inverse design using artificial neural networks
observations: Fig1 reads left-to-right from parameterized particle geometry to model inputs/hidden layers/outputs to optical response. Geometry parameters are attached to the shape, not shown as an abstract parameter list alone.

Fig2 is a compact two-panel evidence group: validation loss versus epochs and model versus simulation spectra; a local inset shows a small wavelength region, and line type distinguishes predictions and closest training data.
application: Use geometry H/t -> completed COMSOL labels -> ridge/GP model -> predicted performance -> held-out physical comparison as the workflow.
Plot prediction versus physical result with a1:1 reference and a separate residual panel; identify held-out structure and condition labels.
do_not_transfer: Our method is GP/ridge, not a DNN; do not draw neural hidden layers or training-epoch loss as if they had been run.
Four H100/t2 condition points remain one independent design; do not present the4 conditions as4 independent structural tests.

immediate_design_recommendations: Use the same upward surface-normal convention in geometry and response panels.
Prefer point-linked controlled comparisons, sparse-data coverage matrices, material-contribution connected plots and prediction/residual panels; show unsolved grid cells blank.
Use panel letters and a single consistent color/marker dictionary. Keep geometry dimensions/units near the object.
Continuous angular lobes and smooth response surfaces require computed density; a visually polished curve cannot supply missing physical evidence.

small_formula_support.supports: Directional Kirchhoff reciprocity for corresponding external direction/polarization channels. Use epsilon_lambda(theta,phi,q)=alpha_lambda(theta,phi,q) with the incoming ray time-reversed relative to outgoing ray, under passive linear reciprocal and isothermal assumptions.

Radiated power integrates Planck spectral radiance multiplied by spectral directional emissivity and projected area cos(theta), over solid angle dOmega=sin(theta)dtheta dphi. Band-averaged emissivity and cone fraction below are transparent definitions derived from that radiometry, not an asserted verbatim metric from the paper.

small_formula_support.reference: Shahriari et al.2016 Proceedings of the IEEE104(1),148–175
small_formula_support.supports: Equations29–30 give GP posterior mean and variance; Bayesian optimization balances information and performance for expensive objective evaluations. Does not prove the present project has completed optimization.

formula_definitions.unpolarized: epsilon_u=(epsilon_s+epsilon_p)/2 for equal-intensity incoherent s/p mixture
formula_definitions.cone_fraction: eta_cone=integral_8^13 integral_Omega_cone epsilon_u B_lambda(T) cos(theta) dOmega dlambda / integral_8^13 integral_hemisphere epsilon_u B_lambda(T) cos(theta) dOmega dlambda
formula_definitions.two_direction_ratio: Q30_0=A_u(10.5um,30deg,30deg)/A_u(10.5um,0deg). This is a project-defined two-direction comparison, not cone fraction, not directivity, and not FWHM.
formula_definitions.MAE_pp: 100/N sum_i |y_i-yhat_i| when y is a0–1 power fraction; grouping held-out complete H/t designs is our anti-leakage validation protocol, not a conclusion taken from a thermal-emission paper.

citation_policy: No citation-count claims are required in the delivered report. Reference original figures as visual precedents; keep a short methods bibliography, not a padded high-citation list.
